fields.Front: What are the two main parts of an object?
fields.Back: Attributes (data members) and behaviors (member functions or methods).

fields.Text: An object's attributes are also called {{c1::data members}}; its behaviors are also called {{c2::member functions or methods}}.

fields.Back: A blueprint or template that defines the properties (attributes) and behaviors (methods) of an object.

fields.Text: An object is an {{c1::instance}} of a class.
fields.Extra: Once a class is defined, you can create objects from it.

fields.Front: If Car is a class, what would objects of that class be?
fields.Back: Specific cars, such as a Ford or a Toyota.

fields.Front: What are attributes in C++ terms, and where are they declared?
fields.Back: Variables that store information about the object; declared inside the class. Example for Car: color, speed, model.

fields.Front: What do methods define? Give the Car examples.
fields.Back: The behavior of an object (what actions it can perform): accelerate(), brake(), getSpeed().

fields.Front: Which members can be accessed by private code?
fields.Back: Only code within the class itself.

fields.Front: What does the public access specifier allow?
fields.Back: Attributes and methods can be accessed from outside the class.

fields.Text: `{{c1::protected}}` members are accessible to derived classes but not from outside the class.
In a C++ class, members declared before any access specifier are {{c1::private}} by default.
A {{c1::constructor}} is a special method that initializes objects of a class; a {{c2::destructor}} cleans up resources when an object is destroyed.

fields.Front: In the slide's Car class, what does Car(std::string carModel, int carYear) do?
fields.Back: It is the constructor: assigns carModel to the member model and carYear to the member year.

fields.Front: Why does myCar.year = 1999; fail to compile for the slide's Car class?
fields.Back: year is declared under private:, so it cannot be accessed from outside the class.

fields.Text: Account(double initialBalance) : balance(initialBalance) {} uses a {{c1::member initializer list}} to initialize balance.

fields.Back: It promises not to modify the object; getters should be const.
